decision.reasoning: The market has no clear direction. The 24h moves are under 1%, which barely covers the ~0.8% round-trip fee. With $20 of capital, trading has negative expected value after fees. Cash doesn't lose value, so I'm holding to keep my runway and will wait for a clearer setup.

I hold nothing yet, and all three pairs are more than 3% above their 50-day SMA, so all three meet the playbook's slow-trend buy rule. SOL is furthest above its SMA (+19.2%, versus +11.6% for ETH and +8.8% for BTC), so I'm buying it with about 30% of equity ($5.99) and keeping about 70% in cash. The small hourly dip doesn't matter under this rule. I'll sell only if SOL closes more than 3% below its 50-day SMA.

I don't hold ETH, and it is 11.6% above its 50-day SMA. That is past the playbook's 3% entry threshold. BTC also qualifies at +9.3%, but ETH is further from its SMA, so the rule says to take ETH. Buying 30% of equity (about 5.99 USD) leaves about 8 USD cash, or roughly 40%, which is well above the 10% minimum. I'm holding SOL, which is +20% vs its SMA, so no sell is triggered.

BTC isn't held and is trading 8.3% above its 50-day SMA, so it passes the playbook's entry test (more than 3% above). Normally I'd put in 30% of equity, about $5.97. I'm spending $5.90 so that about $2.08 stays in cash, which is roughly 10.5% of equity and above the 10% minimum. SOL (+18.5%) and ETH (+10.4%) are already held and still above their SMAs, so I'm keeping both and not adding to either.
